title: Incident Bot v2 — Slack thread mock examples (context cards + actions)
body:
Purpose
- Provide concrete Slack thread examples for Incident Bot v2 “context cards” and interactive actions.
- Use these examples to align on: truncation rules, deep-link parameters, copy-command patterns, degraded-mode behavior, and redaction UX.

Notes / assumptions
- Bot name: incident-bot (posts in #incidents and #eng-oncall threads).
- Trigger: /incident-bot context (manual) OR auto-post when an incident channel is created / Incident declared.
- Cards are posted as Block Kit sections with compact summaries and action buttons.
- “Expand” actions open a Slack modal (pagination for large payloads).
- Deep links go to Redwood Console (dashboards, rollouts, traces) with time window pinned to incident start (-30m, +10m default).
- Tenant/customer safety:
  - Config diff card is tenant-safe by default; redacted fields are shown as REDACTED with an explanation.
  - “Request elevated view” is never a Slack action (avoid secrets over Slack). Instead link to Console with audit + role checks.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
MOCK THREAD 1 — Sev1 Hosted API 503s after deploy (deploy regression)
Channel: #incidents
Thread topic: “Sev1 — hosted-api 503s increasing (us-east-1) — 2025-02-07”

[09:12] Sean Gallagher (IC): Declaring Sev1. Symptoms: spike in 503s + latency. Region looks like us-east-1 only.
[09:13] incident-bot: Posting Incident Context v2 (beta) …

INCIDENT CONTEXT (v2)
Service: hosted-api
Regions: us-east-1 (primary), us-west-2 (baseline)
Time window: 08:40–09:13 (UTC-5)

CARD A — Recent deploys (last 120m)
Summary
- hosted-api deploy started: 08:57
- Rollout phase: 25% → paused
- Image: hosted-api@sha256:7c2f…a19b
- Canary: FAIL (p95 latency +38%, 5xx +1.9%)
- Related changes: PR #29104 “export deploy metadata to incident-bot” (infra), PR #28988 “streaming handler refactor” (app)
Buttons
- Open deploy timeline (Console)
- View canary details
- Copy rollback command
- Show prior deploys

Copy rollback command (button behavior)
- Clicking posts an ephemeral message to the clicker:
  “Copied to clipboard: rwctl deploy rollback --service hosted-api --region us-east-1 --to previous-stable”
  Also includes “Copy again” (idempotent), “Open in runbook” deep link.

CARD B — Error budget / SLO burn
Summary
- SLO: hosted-api availability
- 5xx burn rate: 12.3x (5m), 6.1x (30m)
- p95 latency burn: 4.2x (5m)
Buttons
- Open error budget burn chart
- Open request trace explorer

CARD C — Saturation signals (last 10m)
Summary
- GPU util (p50/p95): 62% / 71% (normal)
- Queue depth (p95): 1.2x baseline (normal)
- Scheduler backpressure: none
- KV cache pressure: low
Interpretation hint (inline)
- “Saturation unlikely; correlate with recent deploy + error signature.”
Buttons
- Open saturation overview
- Open per-pool capacity

CARD D — Error signature (top)
Summary
- 503: upstream reset during streaming handshake
- Spike begins ~08:59 (2m after deploy start)
Buttons
- Open logs (filtered)
- Open traces (sampled)

[09:14] Rafael Mendes (SRE): Deploy correlation is strong. Can someone run rollback for hosted-api us-east-1?
[09:14] Connor O’Brien (releases): On it.
[09:15] Connor O’Brien clicked “Copy rollback command” → (ephemeral to Connor)
[09:16] Connor O’Brien: Rollback initiated. Rollout paused + reverting to previous stable.
[09:18] incident-bot (auto-update): Deploy status changed: rollback 10% complete (us-east-1). Canary: PASS.

UX callouts
- “Recent deploys” card must be first and compact; responders rely on it in first 60s.
- Canary fail highlight should be visually strong (e.g., “FAIL” label + reason).
- Buttons should be 1) open timeline 2) rollback/copy command 3) canary details.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
MOCK THREAD 2 — Sev2 503s after routing policy/config push (config diff)
Channel: #incidents
Thread topic: “Sev2 — elevated 503s after routing policy change — 2025-03-01”

[14:02] Aisha Bello (IC): Seeing 503s on /v1/chat/completions for a subset of tenants. Might be routing policy.
[14:03] incident-bot: Posting Incident Context v2 …

INCIDENT CONTEXT (v2)
Service: router-control-plane
Route: /v1/chat/completions
Regions: eu-west-1 (elevated), us-east-1 (normal)
Tenant: (not specified) — using aggregate view

CARD A — Config changes (last 60m)
Summary
- 1 config push detected at 13:41
- Scope: routing-policy (region=eu-west-1)
- Risky fields changed: fallback_order, model_pin, quota_policy
- Redaction: 3 fields redacted (secrets / customer identifiers)
Buttons
- View safe diff (modal)
- Open diff in Console (audited)
- Copy “show current policy” command
- Retry (if stale)

When “View safe diff (modal)” clicked
Modal title: “Config diff — routing-policy (eu-west-1) — safe view”
Body (paginated)
Page 1/2
- routing.fallback_order:
  - BEFORE: ["gpt-oss-1", "gpt-oss-1-mini"]
  - AFTER:  ["gpt-oss-1-mini", "gpt-oss-1"]
- routing.model_pin:
  - BEFORE: "gpt-oss-1"
  - AFTER:  "gpt-oss-1-mini"
- quota.policy_name:
  - BEFORE: "standard"
  - AFTER:  "standard"

Page 2/2
- feature_flags.enable_streaming_opt:
  - BEFORE: false
  - AFTER: true
- customer_overrides[REDACTED]:
  - BEFORE: REDACTED
  - AFTER:  REDACTED
  (Reason: contains tenant identifiers)
- secrets.api_key_rotation:
  - BEFORE: REDACTED
  - AFTER:  REDACTED
  (Reason: secret-pattern match)

Footer note
“Safe diff hides tenant identifiers and secrets. For full audited view, open in Console (requires on-call role).”

CARD B — Saturation signals
Summary
- GPU util: normal
- Queue depth: normal
- Admission control: elevated rejects (eu-west-1) — 2.4% (baseline 0.1%)
Buttons
- Open admission control dashboard
- Open routing decision log

[14:05] Mina Haddad (routing): That fallback_order flip could be sending more traffic to mini which has lower capacity in eu-west-1.
[14:06] Ravi Menon (graceful degradation): Suggest revert model_pin + fallback order, or increase capacity pool.
[14:06] incident-bot: Suggested actions
- “Revert last routing-policy change (eu-west-1)” (opens Console rollback page)
- “Enable degraded mode: route EU to us-east-1 for pinned tenants” (link to runbook)

UX callouts
- Modal pagination is mandatory; diffs can be long.
- “Copy show current policy command” should be safe and not include tenant IDs:
  rwctl config get --scope routing-policy --region eu-west-1
- “Open diff in Console” is the only path to any privileged view; Slack stays safe.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
MOCK THREAD 3 — Sev1 EU regional capacity saturation (saturation signals + fallback context)
Channel: #incidents
Thread topic: “Sev1 — eu-west-1 capacity saturation, latency spikes — 2025-03-10”

[19:22] Jacob Stein: Latency p95 doubled in eu-west-1. Queue depth rising. Dedicated + Hosted both impacted.
[19:22] incident-bot: Posting Incident Context v2 …

INCIDENT CONTEXT (v2)
Services: hosted-api, dedicated-gateway
Region: eu-west-1

CARD A — Saturation overview (last 15m)
Summary (eu-west-1)
- GPU util p95: 97% (HIGH)
- Queue depth p95: 4.8x baseline (HIGH)
- KV cache evictions: 3.1x baseline (HIGH)
- Scheduler backpressure: active (admission control engaged)
Badges
- “Saturation likely primary cause”
Buttons
- Open saturation dashboard
- Open per-pool breakdown
- Copy “shed load” command

Copy “shed load” command (button)
Ephemeral output:
- rwctl routing set --region eu-west-1 --policy degraded --reason "incident" --ttl 60m
- Notes: “Applies only to eligible traffic tiers; does not override tenant pins.”

CARD B — Routing / fallback context (tenant-safe)
Summary
- Current policy: standard
- Fallback enabled: YES
- Cross-region failover: DISABLED (hosted-api)
- Dedicated isolation: ENABLED
Buttons
- Open routing policy (Console)
- Open degraded mode runbook

CARD C — Recent deploys
Summary
- No deploys in last 120m for services in eu-west-1
Buttons
- Show last successful deploy

[19:24] Priya Natarajan: We should flip degraded mode for hosted to reduce pressure + keep dedicated isolated.
[19:25] Rafael Mendes: Agree. Use TTL 60m; keep audit trail.
[19:26] incident-bot (degraded-mode confirmation): Degraded mode toggled for eu-west-1 (requested by @rafael.mendes). TTL: 60m.

UX callouts
- Saturation card should include explicit thresholds and a “HIGH” indicator when crossing.
- Routing/fallback card is critical to avoid accidental changes that violate dedicated isolation.
- We need “copy command” variants for both rwctl and Console (some teams don’t have CLI set up during incident).

-------------------------------------------------------------------
MOCK THREAD 4 — Sev1 Streaming disconnects (telemetry timeouts + degraded-mode behavior)
Channel: #incidents
Thread topic: “Sev1 — streaming disconnects, bot queries slow — 2025-03-14”

[07:48] Miles Thornton (IC): Clients reporting streaming disconnects. Also noticing internal dashboards are slow.
[07:49] incident-bot: Posting Incident Context v2 …

INCIDENT CONTEXT (v2)
Service: hosted-api
Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming)
Region: us-east-1

CARD A — Error signature
Summary
- streaming_disconnect_rate: 3.8% (baseline 0.2%)
- dominant error: client EOF / upstream timeout
Buttons
- Open streaming health dashboard
- Open logs (filtered)

CARD B — Telemetry queries (status)
Summary
- Live telemetry query: TIMEOUT (after 2.5s)
- Using cached snapshot: 07:45–07:47
Buttons
- Retry live query
- Open dashboard links (no query)
- View manual steps

When “View manual steps” clicked (modal)
Title: “Manual steps (when bot is degraded)”
- 1) Open Console → Streaming health dashboard (link)
- 2) Check recent deploy timeline for hosted-api (link)
- 3) Run: rwctl incidents snapshot --service hosted-api --region us-east-1 --window 30m
- 4) If query system overloaded: do not spam retries; coordinate through IC.

[07:50] Logan Wright: Telemetry query service is overloaded; please avoid rapid retries.
[07:50] incident-bot: Rate limiting enabled for this thread (1 retry / 60s). Showing links only.

UX callouts
- Degraded-mode message must be explicit and calm: “links-only, cached snapshot, retry later”.
- “Retry live query” must be guarded (coalesced + rate-limited) and show countdown until next allowed retry.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
MOCK THREAD 5 — “Expand diff” + “Open in Console” interplay (redaction warning UX)
Channel: #eng-oncall
Thread topic: “Example: config diff redaction”

[11:10] Devon Price: Testing config diff view. Does the redaction warning feel clear enough?
[11:10] incident-bot: Config diff available (safe view)

CARD — Config changes
Summary
- 6 fields changed
- 2 redacted (secrets)
Buttons
- View safe diff (modal)
- Open in Console (audited)

When user clicks “Open in Console (audited)”
- Bot posts ephemeral message:
  “This link may display privileged fields depending on your role. Access is audited. If denied, request break-glass via on-call policy.”

Desired behavior
- Slack should never show the privileged values; only safe diff is in Slack.
- Console should show “accessed via incident-bot” in audit context.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
Proposed button taxonomy (keep consistent across cards)
- View/Expand actions (Slack):
  - “View safe diff” (modal)
  - “Show prior deploys” (modal)
  - “View manual steps” (modal)
- Deep links (Console):
  - “Open deploy timeline”
  - “Open saturation dashboard”
  - “Open error budget burn chart”
  - “Open traces” / “Open logs”
- Copy-to-clipboard actions:
  - “Copy rollback command”
  - “Copy show current policy command”
  - “Copy shed load command”

Truncation + summary rules (draft)
- Card summaries should be 5–8 lines max.
- Use badges: PASS/FAIL/HIGH/TIMEOUT.
- Always include time window and region(s).
- Prefer “top 3 changes” in summary; remainder in modal.
- Diffs in Slack must be normalized (stable ordering) to reduce noise.

Open questions
- Do we want the bot to auto-post “Suggested actions” (as in Mock #2) or keep to context-only to avoid oversteering?
- For copy commands, should we prefer rwctl only, or provide “kubectl/console” variants based on responder role?
- Best default time window: -30m/+10m vs -60m/+10m? (SRE preference seems -30m.)

TODOs
- Align deep-link format with Console team (query params for service/region/route/window).
- Validate modal pagination behavior for very large diffs (1000+ lines) and ensure graceful fallback.
- Add an explicit “Report missing context” button that opens a prefilled Linear issue (or posts a thread template).
